annotations.text:
The screens set, ADR-0046. Read across, then down.

Row 1: the two places that hold everything — Home, and Inventory beside the drawing you already approved.
Row 2: the crossing between them, and the patching surface at faceplate zoom.
Row 3: undo that records, and notes plus a maintenance record in the one editor.
Row 4: the two admin surfaces reached from the account chip.
Row 5: walkthrough, sketched only.

Four boards move. Each motion plays once on its event in the product; here it replays so you can watch it.

The rule every board shares: the inspector on the drawing and the page in the inventory are one component. Same fields, same code. That is what makes 'edited from either' true, and why inventory never grows a second detail pane.
Every name, version, time and hash on these boards is a sample. Counts, models and positions in the product come from the graph and the catalogue and are never typed.
